summary.title: Being visible
summary.one_liner: Learn why internal and external visibility matter for reaching a Staff-plus engineering role, and which concrete activities build a good reputation without overspending organizational bandwidth.
takeaways: Working on your company's top priorities is the single best way to become visible internally.
Executive visibility, especially with your manager's manager, matters most because those leaders often approve Staff-plus promotions.
Practical internal tactics include writing long-lived design docs, leading architecture reviews, sharing weekly work notes, and contributing to the company blog.
External visibility (talks, podcasts, writing, mailing lists) can help create a niche, but is not required for Staff-plus success.
Treat visibility as a transient currency: do the minimum needed to clear the promotion threshold, then focus on learning and development.
summary.summary: This essay from the staffeng.com guides argues that reputation and visibility are a major part of reaching a Staff-plus role, alongside luck and work. It explains why leaders need to know and trust candidates, and it separates internal visibility (working on company priorities, writing documents, leading reviews, sharing notes) from executive visibility and external visibility (talks, podcasts, books, newsletters). It closes by advising people to use the promotion packet to judge whether visibility is actually a blocker, and to avoid over-investing in it beyond that point.
